node.title: Re: AUTOLOAD vs. DESTROY...
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Having written a "do everything" object like this myself ([https://github.com/haukex/emperl5/blob/webperl_v0.09-beta/ext/WebPerl/lib/WebPerl.pm#L246|WebPerl::JSObject]), I can confirm that there are some methods you won't be able to override, and some you probably shouldn't (e.g. those from [doc://UNIVERSAL]). IMHO, you probably should just bite the bullet and document for your users that not all method calls will be AUTOLOADed. Either that, or reconsider using AUTOLOAD in the first place - for example, I wrote [mod://IPC::Run3::Shell] because the AUTOLOADing behavior of [mod://Shell] is a bit too dangerous, or I wrote [mod://Util::H2O] to provide protection against typos when accessing hashes. OTOH, for a dynamic object, a purely hashref- and arrayref-based interface might make sense from a user's point of view.

However, methods like FETCH and FIRSTKEY shouldn't be a problem ([https://webperl.zero-g.net/democode/perleditor.html#%7B%22cmdline%22%3A%22perl%20foo.pl%22%2C%22script%22%3A%22use%20warnings%3B%5Cnuse%20strict%3B%5Cnuse%20WebPerl%20'js'%3B%5Cnuse%20Data%3A%3ADumper%3B%5Cn%24Data%3A%3ADumper%3A%3AUseqq%3D1%3B%5Cn%5Cnmy%20%24x%20%3D%20js(%7Ba%3D%3Esub%7B%5B%5C%22a%5C%22%2C%5C%22b%5C%22%2C%5C%22c%5C%22%5D%7D%7D)%3B%5Cn%23%20%24x%20is%20now%20a%20%5C%22do%20everything%5C%22%20object%5Cn%5Cnprint%20Dumper(%20%24x-%3Ea-%3E%5B1%5D%20)%3B%20%20%23%20%5C%22b%5C%22%5Cneval%20%7B%5Cn%5Ctprint%20Dumper(%20%24x-%3EFETCH(1)%20)%3B%20%20%23%20nope%5Cn%7D%20or%20warn%20%24%40%3B%5Cneval%20%7B%5Cn%5Ctprint%20Dumper(%20%24x-%3Ea-%3EFETCH(1)%20)%3B%20%20%23%20nope%5Cn%7D%20or%20warn%20%24%40%3B%22%2C%22script_fn%22%3A%22foo.pl%22%2C%22autorun%22%3Atrue%7D|WebPerl example], requires a modern browser). You haven't shown us an [id://1177642|SSCCE], but I suspect that perhaps you're using a single class to handle the AUTOLOAD and the tied interfaces as well, which I would recommend against; you should use separate classes for each of the [doc://tie]d types.

Also, a word of warning: it's possible to make an interface "too clever" such that it gets so complex that only the author will understand it ("It's so simple! Just press Ctrl+Shift+\ while clicking the middle mouse button!"). Consider as one counterexample the method-based API of [mod://Hash::Ordered], which some would consider that a quite clean API. Of course an API like the one you are designing could be made quite clean as well if you don't overload it too much, I don't know since you haven't described the whole thing, but it is something to keep in mind.

Minor edits.
